items.title: Muru
items.raw_text: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. items.title: Research Tools: University of Richmond Distant Viewing Lab Releases DataReel, a New AI Tool for Film Research
items.raw_text: From the University of Richmond: University of Richmond’s Distant Viewing Lab has released DataReel , a new open access, AI-powered tool that helps researchers analyze films. DataReel uses AI models to automatically capture data from over 2,000 films, presenting it in an interactive, visual format. It measures descriptions of scenes, the characters onscreen, shot length, framing distance (close-ups or long shots), how many people are on screen, how much the camera moves, and how much of the film is speech or music. The patterns could help scholars explore questions such as how close-ups influence psychological engagement, how pacing affects narrative tension, and how visual and audio techniques vary across genres. The Distant Viewing Lab is directed by Taylor Arnold, professor of data science and statistics, and Lauren Tilton, professor of digital humanities and director of UR’s Center for Liberal Arts and AI. “Current AI models can analyze two-dimensional images, but not how or why they were filmed in a particular way,” said Tilton. “Our research will further the ability of AI not only to recognize objects in moving images but also to analyze patterns, an important step forward for all scholarly communities working with digital media.” Support for this project was awarded by Schmidt Sciences and includes collaboration with UC Berkeley and Bowdoin College. items.title: The Biodiversity Heritage Library unlocks centuries of biodiversity knowledge
items.raw_text: Bringing the world’s biodiversity literature together The Biodiversity Heritage Library (BHL) continues to expand access to historical biodiversity literature and archival collections, connecting centuries of scientific knowledge with contemporary research and conservation efforts. During a the November 17th, 2026 webinar Unlocking Biodiversity Data: From Local Collections to Global Datasets , Colleen Funkhouser, Managing Director of the BHL, outlined the library’s work as the world’s largest open-access digital library for biodiversity literature and archives. Established in 2006, the BHL brings together natural history museums, botanical institutions, universities, and libraries through a global consortium. Its collection now contains more than 64 million pages, representing over 200,000 titles and 323,000 volumes dating from the 15th through the 21st century. These collections preserve original species descriptions, historical distribution records, climate observations, scientific illustrations and accounts of expeditions. Through taxonomic name recognition, researchers – and the general public – can search scientific names across the collection, which has indexed more than 276 million instances of taxonomic names. The BHL also provides application programming interface (APIs), downloadable publications, high-resolution images, optical character recognition (OCR) text, and article-level indexing. items.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
items.raw_text: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
items.raw_text: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. items.title: Amazon is complaining about NYC Council on shipping labels, too
items.raw_text: Amazon is getting increasingly aggressive about not wanting to employ its army of delivery workers. | Photo: The Verge Amazon is leaving no venue unexplored in its fight against the New York City Council and the Delivery Protection Act . The company is now putting labels on shipments claiming that the Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order. The Delivery Protection Act would effectively ban the sort of third-party arrangements Amazon currently uses to deliver many packages, including small companies and independent contractors. Last-mile delivery firms operating warehouses would need to be licensed by the city and directly employ their workers. items.title: Amazon’s first digital photo frame is up to 50 percent off for Black Friday
items.raw_text: Amazon only announced its first digital photo frame less than a month ago, but it’s already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. You can currently grab the Alexa Photo Frame at Amazon and Best Buy starting at $114 ($115 off), making it a great holiday gift for anyone who loves displaying family photos. If you prefer the walnut trim over the birch or standard black models, it’s also on sale at Best Buy for $134.99 ($95 off) — which, like with the others, is the first discount we’ve seen. Amazon Alexa Photo Frame Where to Buy: $229.99 $114.99 at Amazon (birch) $199.99 $114.99 at Best Buy (black) $229.99 $134.99 at Best Buy (walnut) The Alexa Photo Frame features a 10-inch, semi-matte touchscreen that’s designed to make digital photos look more natural, with built-in light sensors that automatically adjust brightness throughout the day. It displays images from Amazon Photos, which supports uploads from both iOS and Android devices, including photos stored in iCloud. You can choose which people or albums to display, or let Alexa Plus do the work, which often results in photos based on your facial expression, the season, and even the lighting. You can also search for specific photos with voice commands, letting you easily pull up images of your first dog, your child as a baby, and other shots without having to scroll endlessly through years of photos yourself. items.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
items.raw_text: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years. All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets. You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure , something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. items.title: Our go-to earbuds for taking calls have fallen to their lowest price to date
items.raw_text: The Liberty 5 Pro are Soundcore’s most ambitious earbuds to date. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge If you’re looking for a new pair of earbuds, the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro are on sale for $129.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart right now. That’s the lowest price we’ve seen for Anker’s excellent wireless earbuds, which normally retail for $169.99 and come in four colors (black, white, blue, and pink) all of which are discounted through November 30th as part of Anker’s ongoing Black Friday promo . Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Where to Buy: $169.99 $129.99 at Amazon $169.99 $129.99 at Walmart $169.99 $129.99 at Best Buy While the Liberty 5 Pro have a number of great features — including support LDAC for high-res audio and an IP55 dust and water resistance rating — the call quality is what stands out. The microphone does an impressive job cutting out background noise, and my colleague John Higgins praised the Liberty 5 Pro for filtering out emergency vehicles, arborists cutting tree branches, and even loud children. The active noise cancellation is excellent, which helps when you’re trying to hear someone on the other end of the phone whose earbuds aren’t as clear as yours. The charging case also features a handy 0.96-inch screen, so you can adjust the ANC and sound profile on the fly. Read our Anker Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro review .

items.title: Giving its AI more to read made T-Mobile's answers worse
items.raw_text: T-Mobile's first attempt to give its AI customer service agents enough context backfired. The agents had access to a large body of support documentation, but conflicting instructions could send them down the wrong path for a customer's request, according to CIO Jeff Simon at VentureBeat's Agentic Infrastructure Stack Summit in October. A subsequent knowledge graph proved too slow and difficult for agents to navigate. Read more
